question: given an opinion and the speaker's candidate units, which representation ranks a supporting passage first

masked_quotes.candidates: the row's candidate list (the speaker's per-turn sentences), checked against the list rebuilt from the LDS with resolve_hearing_people
masked_quotes.relevance: a unit is relevant when it contains a sentence listed in target_indices (the sentences that agree with the silver target sentence enclosing the trusted quote prefix)

filters: at least one sentence unit of the speaker overlaps a located chunk segment
nli.candidates: rebuilt from person_resolution.turn_indices with split_into_turns and split_sentences on each turn, the resolution rechecked with resolve_person_speech on the NLI person name
nli.relevance: a unit is relevant when its character span overlaps the recorded span (chosen occurrence) of any segment of any located chunk of the opinion; the label says the opinion was judged inferable from the four retrieved chunks together (retrieved_context_entailment), not that each overlapping unit supports it

definitions.rank: 1-based position of the first relevant unit in the retriever's order
definitions.rank_optimistic: 1 + number of non-relevant units scored strictly above the best relevant
definitions.rank_pessimistic: 1 + number of non-relevant units scored at or above the best relevant
definitions.acc_at_k: share of queries whose rank is at most k
definitions.random_acc_at_1: mean over queries of n_relevant / n_units, the acc@1 of a uniform pick
definitions.acc_at_1_minus_random: acc@1 minus random_acc_at_1, comparable across unit sizes
definitions.top1_chars: characters of the top-1 unit, the evidence the retriever would hand over
definitions.ci: percentile interval over bootstrap replicates that resample whole hearings
definitions.mcnemar: exact two-sided binomial test on the queries where exactly one of the baseline and the other retriever has the relevant unit at rank 1; it treats queries as independent, so the hearing-bootstrap interval of the acc@1 difference is reported next to it
definitions.mrr_test: two-sided sign-flip permutation test that flips whole hearings

units.definitions: sentence: one candidate sentence; windowN: N consecutive candidate sentences of one turn, stride 1, a turn with fewer than N sentences gives one unit with all of them, text joined by a space, span from the first sentence start to the last sentence end; turn: the whole turn text (whitespace normalized, including stage directions and parts shorter than a sentence), only turns with at least one candidate sentence

serafim_335m.card_notes: config_sentence_transformers.json: prompts {} and default_prompt_name null, so no prefix; modules: Transformer (BertModel, hidden 1024) + mean Pooling, no Normalize module; sentence_bert_config.json max_seq_length 128 (production value, kept so vectors equal the build_udvs cache); trained with AnglELoss on STS.

serafim_335m_ir.card_notes: prompts {} and default_prompt_name null, no prefix in the card usage; Transformer (BertModel, 1024) + mean Pooling, no Normalize; max_seq_length 128; train-config.yaml: GISTEmbedLoss on unicamp-dl/mmarco portuguese pairs, base bertimbau-335m.

serafim_900m.card_notes: prompts {} and default_prompt_name null, no prefix; Transformer (DebertaV2Model, hidden 1536) + mean Pooling, no Normalize; max_seq_length 128; train-config.yaml base albertina-900m-ptpt (European Portuguese base), CoSENT on STS.

e5_large.card_notes: README: each input must start with 'query: ' or 'passage: '; 'query: '/'passage: ' for asymmetric passage retrieval, 'query: ' on both sides for symmetric similarity; the asymmetric pair is used because the query (an opinion summary) and the passages (transcript speech) differ in length and register. No config_sentence_transformers.json prompts in the snapshot, so the prefixes are prepended to the text here. Modules: XLMRobertaModel (1024) + mean Pooling + Normalize; max_seq_length 512.

bge_m3.card_notes: README: 'the BGE-M3 model no longer requires adding instructions to the queries'; dense vectors from sentence-transformers: XLMRobertaModel (1024) + CLS Pooling + Normalize; max_seq_length 8192 (native, kept; a batch never exceeds token_budget tokens, so one 8192-token sequence runs alone). Sparse and ColBERT heads (sparse_linear.pt, colbert_linear.pt) are not used.

mpnet.card_notes: no prompts in config_sentence_transformers.json and no prefix in the card; XLMRobertaModel (768) + mean Pooling, no Normalize; max_seq_length 128; paraphrase model (symmetric).

minilm.card_notes: no prompts and no prefix; BertModel (384) + mean Pooling, no Normalize; max_seq_length 128; paraphrase model (symmetric).

hybrid_rrf.choice: declared before any retrieval result was computed: BM25 fitted on the speaker's units (the sparse design the benchmarks were built around) fused with the production encoder, so the hybrid measures what lexical evidence adds to the encoder already in use; another dense component may only be chosen on train

rerank_bge.card_notes: config.json: XLMRobertaForSequenceClassification with id2label {0: LABEL_0}, a single relevance logit (higher = more relevant), no sbert_ce_default_activation_function; README scores with max_length=512 and maps to [0, 1] with sigmoid only optionally. The raw logit is used (activation Identity), which gives the same order as the sigmoid without saturated ties. No query instruction for this normal (non-LLM) reranker.

rerank_mmarco.card_notes: config.json: XLMRobertaForSequenceClassification, id2label {0: LABEL_0}, a single logit, sbert_ce_default_activation_function Identity; tokenizer model_max_length 512; trained on machine-translated mMARCO (includes pt).

evaluation.multiple_comparisons: holm, per benchmark and split group, across every compared (retriever, unit) pair, separately for the McNemar and the MRR tests
evaluation.tie_policy: order by score descending, candidate index ascending on ties (the argmax rule of the UDV builder); rank_optimistic and rank_pessimistic bound the rank of the first relevant unit over every tie order

cache.batch_size_note: batch sizes measured on 2026-09-22 (Apple M5, MPS, fp32, serafim-335m, 512 sentences): 16 to 32 give about 2.1k tokens/s, 64 about 1.0k and 256 about 0.55k; the batch size changes vectors only at float rounding level

queue.plan: priority order under the measured MPS throughput: every retriever on the sentence unit (E1) and the turn unit, the four units (E2) for the production encoder, the hybrid and the small reranker; windows for other dense models and the large reranker beyond sentences are left for a later step chosen on train
